paper.title: LIMO: Less is More for Reasoning

result.summary: 本文挑战了复杂推理必须依赖海量训练数据的假设，提出 Less-Is-More Reasoning (LIMO) 假说：在预训练已编码丰富领域知识的基础模型中，复杂推理可通过少量精心设计的认知过程示范被激发 [abstract][S1.p3]。作者通过多层筛选构建了仅 800 条样本的 LIMO 数据集，并对 Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct 进行简单 SFT [S1.p4]。LIMO 在 AIME24 上达到 63.3%、MATH500 上达到 95.6%，超过此前微调模型，且仅使用其 1% 的训练数据 [abstract]。LIMO 还展现出较强的分布外泛化能力，在多样基准上取得 45.8% 的绝对提升，优于使用 100 倍数据训练的模型 [abstract]。

research_question.text: 本文要解决的问题是：复杂推理是否真的需要海量训练数据，还是可以通过少量高质量样本激发。原文指出，传统范式通常基于两个假设：掌握复杂认知过程需要大量监督示范，且监督微调主要导致记忆而非真正泛化 [S1.p1]。作者认为这种数据密集型范式可能不再必要，因为现代基础模型在预训练中已包含大量数学内容，挑战已从知识获取转变为知识激发 [S1.p2]。

evidence.quote: The resulting paradigm typically involves training on tens or hundreds of thousands of examples, based on two fundamental assumptions

first, that mastering such complex cognitive processes requires extensive supervised demonstrations, and second, that supervised fine-tuning leads primarily to memorization rather than true generalization.
We argue this data-intensive paradigm may no longer be necessary.
Contemporary LLMs may already possess rich mathematical knowledge, transforming the challenge from knowledge acquisition to knowledge elicitation.

method.text: 作者提出 LIMO 假说，认为复杂推理的激发阈值取决于模型参数中是否潜在具备前置知识，以及少量示例能否有效示范解题过程并鼓励扩展推理 [S1.p3]。方法上，作者从大规模 QA 池出发，先进行粗粒度难度过滤，再进行细粒度难度评估和知识点多样化，同时按逻辑连贯性、步骤清晰度和解答正确性筛选推理链，最终得到 800 条训练样本 [S1.p4]。随后使用简单监督微调，在 Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct 上训练 [S1.p4]。

evidence.quote: We propose the Less-Is-More Reasoning (LIMO) Hypothesis, identifying two critical factors determining the elicitation threshold for complex reasoning

(1) the latent presence of prerequisite knowledge within the model’s parameters, and (2) the effectiveness of minimal exemplars in demonstrating problem-solving processes that encourage extended deliberation.

Starting from a large pool of QA pairs, we implement a multi-layered filtering system: first conducting coarse difficulty filtering to eliminate trivial problems, then fine-grained difficulty assessment to identify challenging questions, followed by knowledge point diversification to ensure comprehensive coverage.
Simultaneously, we filter reasoning chains based on logical coherence, step-by-step clarity, and solution accuracy.
This meticulous process yields a compact yet potent dataset of just 800 training samples.
With simple supervised fine-tuning (SFT) using only this curated dataset based on Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct

experiments.text: 实验在域内基准 AIME24、MATH500 和 AMC23 上评估，并在分布外基准 OlympiadBench、CHMath、Gaokao、Kaoyan、GradeSchool、Minerva 和 GPQA 上评估 [S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1][S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1]。评估使用 pass@1 指标和零样本思维链设置；较大基准使用贪心解码单样本，小于 50 题的基准生成 4 个样本并计算无偏 pass@1 [S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1]。对比基线包括 OpenAI-o1-preview、QwQ-32B-Preview、Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct，以及用 OpenThoughts-114k 和 NuminaMath-100k 微调的模型 [S6.SS1.p1][S6.SS1.p2]。

evidence.quote: Our primary evaluation suite includes several well-established mathematical competitions and benchmarks: the American Invitational Mathematics Examination (AIME24), MATH500, and the American Mathematics Competitions (AMC23).
First, we include diverse mathematical competitions like OlympiadBench to test performance on different mathematical challenges.

Second, to minimize data contamination, we construct novel multilingual benchmarks using recent examination problems: CHMath (2024 Chinese High School Mathematics League), Gaokao (China’s 2024 College Entrance Exam), Kaoyan (Chinese Graduate School Entrance Exams), and GradeSchool (our new elementary mathematics benchmark).

Third, we incorporate multi-disciplinary benchmarks including Minerva (undergraduate-level STEM) and GPQA to evaluate the transfer of mathematical reasoning skills to broader contexts beyond our training domain.
We evaluate performance using the pass@1 metric in a zero-shot chain-of-thought setting across all benchmarks.
For smaller benchmarks (less than 50 problems: AIME24, AMC23, and CHMath), we generate 4 samples (temperature=0.6) and calculate the unbiased pass@1 metric.

These include OpenAI-o1-preview, a large language model that has demonstrated advanced mathematical reasoning abilities across various complex tasks; QwQ-32B-Preview, a model specifically designed for mathematical problem-solving with strong reasoning capabilities; and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct, which serves as our base model for comparative analysis.

These comparative datasets include OpenThoughts-114k, a synthetic reasoning dataset containing 114k examples covering mathematics, science, coding, and puzzles, with solutions following a structured reasoning format generated by DeepSeek-R1; and NuminaMath-100k, a randomly selected 100k subset of NuminaMath-CoT

findings.text: 在域内任务上，LIMO 在 AIME24 达到 63.3%，超过 QwQ-32B-Preview 的 50.0% 和 OpenAI-o1-preview 的 44.6%；在 MATH500 达到 95.6%，超过 QwQ-32B-Preview 的 89.8% 和 OpenAI-o1-preview 的 85.5%；在 AMC23 达到 96.3%，高于 QwQ-32B-Preview 的 83.6% [S6.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1]。在分布外任务上，LIMO 在 OlympiadBench 达到 67.6%，高于 QwQ-32B-Preview 的 58.5% 和基座模型的 45.3%；在 CHMath 为 84.2% 对 68.5%，在 GradeSchool 为 76.2% 对 63.8%；在 GPQA 上达到 70.7%，接近 OpenAI-o1-preview 的 73.3% [S6.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1]。与更大数据集相比，NuminaMath-100k 出现显著退化（32.3% 对基座模型 49.9%），OpenThoughts-114k 为 58.3%，而 LIMO 的 800 题达到 78.1% [S6.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1]。LIMO 在所有基准上的平均性能最高，为 78.1% [S6.SS2.SSS0.Px4.p1]。

evidence.quote: For AIME24, LIMO achieves 63.3% accuracy, outperforming QwQ-32B-Preview (50.0%) and OpenAI-o1-preview (44.6%) by significant margins.
On MATH500, LIMO achieves a notable 95.6% accuracy, surpassing QwQ-32B-Preview (89.8%) and OpenAI-o1-preview (85.5%).
The performance gap is even more pronounced on AMC23, where LIMO reaches 96.3% accuracy compared to QwQ-32B-Preview’s 83.6%.
On OlympiadBench, LIMO achieves 67.6% accuracy, significantly outperforming QwQ-32B-Preview (58.5%) and the base model (45.3%).
Similar improvements are observed on other challenging benchmarks such as CHMath (84.2% vs 68.5%) and GradeSchool (76.2% vs 63.8%).
Notably, LIMO maintains competitive performance even on GPQA, where it achieves 70.7% accuracy, close to OpenAI-o1-preview’s leading score of 73.3%.

NuminaMath-100k shows significant degradation (32.3% vs. base model’s 49.9%) due to uncurated reasoning chains, while OpenThoughts-114k achieves suboptimal results (58.3%) probably due to unfocused problem selection.

In contrast, LIMO’s carefully curated 800 problems yield superior performance (78.1%), demonstrating that targeted selection are more crucial than data quantity for developing robust reasoning capabilities.
LIMO achieves the highest average performance of 78.1% across all benchmarks, substantially outperforming OpenAI-o1-preview, QwQ-32B-Preview, and other baselines.

limitations.text: 作者指出，尽管 800 条样本即可激发竞赛级数学推理，但维持有效性能的下界仍是一个开放问题 [S6.SS3.SSS5.p1]。此外，作者提到未来工作可以探索主动学习策略以进一步优化样本效率 [S6.SS3.SSS5.p2]。

evidence.quote: Our experiments reveal that a surprisingly small number (i.e. 800) of samples can elicit competition-level mathematical reasoning, though the lower bound for maintaining effective performance remains an open question.
Future work could explore active learning strategies to further optimize sample efficiency.
